sample_space.description: 988 TeO2 bolometer crystals, 5 x 5 x 5 cm3, 750 g each (742 kg total), in 19 copper-framed towers of 13 floors x 4 crystals, each crystal with an NTD thermistor and heater; operated at ~10 mK (8 mK base). Quote: 'CUORE is composed of 988 5 x 5 x 5 cm3 TeO2 crystals, each having a mass of 750 g' and 'The crystals are arranged into 19 copper-framed towers, with each tower consisting of 13 floors of 4 crystals' (https://arxiv.org/pdf/1710.07988). Tower height is not published in the sources checked.

moving_parts.quote: This valve makes 0.7 revolutions per second ... results in pressure waves with a frequency that depends on the PT model and which is 1.4 Hz for the CUORE PTs

moving_parts.rate: five PT compressors ~15 m from the 300 K plate
moving_parts.quote: The compressors are located ~15 m away from the 300 K plate and are supported by a metallic structure connected to the concrete ground

moving_parts.rate: 3He/4He mixture circulation, up to >= 8 mmol/s with both condensing lines
moving_parts.quote: The maximum flow rate using both lines is >= 8 mmol s-1

moving_parts.rate: detector on Minus K isolators, 0.5 Hz cut-off; external lead on a movable platform
moving_parts.quote: This behavior favors very low natural frequencies for the spring-mass system, with a cut-off frequency of close to 0.5 Hz

geometry.notes: Six nested vessels: 300 K, 40 K, 4 K, Still (~0.8-0.9 K), HEX (~50 mK), MC (~10 mK). Vessel (shield) heights/diameters, Table II of arXiv:1904.05745: 300 K 1603x2620 mm; 40 K 1503x2765 mm; 4 K 1363x2471 mm; Still 1110x1850 mm; HEX 1020x1650 mm; MC 940x1365 mm. Inner Lead Shield (Roman lead, 1157 mm diam x 1568 mm, 60 mm thick, 3920 kg) between 4 K and Still; Top Lead (900 mm diam x 300 mm, 2110 kg) below MC plate above TSP. Cooling: five Cryomech PT415-RM (32 W at 45 K, 1.2 W at 4.2 K nominal each) on 40 K/4 K plates plus a custom dilution unit (~3-6 uW at 10 mK; 2 mW at 100 mK). 300 K plate suspended from a 4.7 m x 4.1 m steel I-beam Main Support Plate; total cold mass >15 t (LNGS page). Plate-to-plate distances Table I: 300K-40K 195 mm, 300K-4K 198 mm, 300K-Still 287 mm, Still-HEX 112 mm, HEX-MC 202 mm. Catalog file lists only the LNGS page; detailed numbers come from the collaboration's cryostat paper (Alduino et al., Cryogenics 2019, arXiv:1904.05745), first-results PRL (arXiv:1710.07988) and the PT noise-cancellation paper (arXiv:1712.02753). stages.name: Cold mass test (measurement) vessel, LN2 at ambient pressure
stages.quote: Test temperatures are as follows: cold-boundary temperature (CBT) 78 K, warm-boundary temperature (WBT) 293 K, temperature difference (AT) 216 K, and mean temperature 186K.

stages.quote: During operation, all three vessels are kept filled with liquid nitrogen near saturation at ambient pressure (temperature ≈77.4 K).

diameter_or_width.location: cold mass diameter = specimen inner diameter

windows.quote: has a lid 104 with three feedthroughs 106 a - 106 c capable of filling and venting a cryogenic fluid (e.g., liquid nitrogen (LN2)), a view port 108 , auxiliary ports 110 for instrumentation, and a pair of lifting supports (handling lugs) 112 .

geometry.notes: Cryostat-100 is a vertical cylindrical LN2 boil-off calorimeter, not a sample cryostat: the 'stages' are the LN2-filled cold mass (78 K cold boundary) and the 293 K heater sleeve warm boundary; the 'sample' is an annular insulation shell wrapped around the cold mass. Published dimensions cover only the cold mass (167/168 mm diameter, 1 m / 1026 mm with guards; test-chamber effective length 575 mm per patent: 'using an effective length of the cold mass of 575 mm, the mean surface area for heat transfer through a typical 25-mm thick insulation test article is 0.35 m 2'). The vacuum canister's outer size is not published anywhere found, so the outer block carries cold-mass numbers with that stated; the canister must be modelled as a slightly larger stainless cylinder with a domed lid without quoting a dimension. Vacuum range: below 1x10-5 torr to 760 torr (NTRS 20150011030). Cold mass suspended by six Kevlar threads ('six KEVLAR threads with hooks and hardware for attachment and length adjustment', patent); CO2-filled vapor-pocket disks separate guard and test vessels; bake-out heaters on the canister exterior. Sources: KSC-TOPS-79 (cache 8a6b708eed0b8339), NTRS 20150011030 (c582e9d07eb670ef), NTRS 20100005254 tech brief (a6e9f3182a5f41ae), NTRS 20130012853 bulk-fill paper (3340971823e78180), US 8,628,238 B2 (2db63b0b75f42b79).

geometry.notes: Bespoke NPL facility, not a catalogue product. Sources: (1) NPL cryogenic testing services page: helium cooling with active temperature control for ~20 K, capabilities to 4 K, 'bespoke LN2 and LHe cryostats', specimens up to ~250 mm. (2) CEC/ICMC 2025 abstract M4Or1B-02 (Spetsieris, Gower, Giannis, NPL): wet-bath cryostat; 77 K by submerging the rig in LN2, 20 K by controllably boiling LHe in the test dewar with heating elements. (3) ECCM21 2024 grip paper (eprintspublications.npl.co.uk/10069): cylindrical cryogenic grips rated 100 or 250 kN, steel pull-rods, 60 kN preload, 250x25x5 mm coupons, three Type-T thermocouples, 2 mm/min displacement control, 'liquid flow cryostat' submerged in LN2 at 77 K. (4) NPL Report MAT 102 (2022) is a REQUIREMENTS specification for the planned system, not an as-built description: servo-hydraulic frame with top-mounted actuator, 250 kN load cell, telescopic lift cylinders for the dewar top, T-slotted platen, ~20-25 litre double-wall dewar (LN2 jacket around LHe inner), top-flange inlet/outlet ports, thermal baffles, 20-300 K control with ±2 K accuracy; use these only as 'design intent'. Rendering guidance: vertical dewar on a load-frame base, pull-rod from a top actuator, coupon in bath; LHe liquid plus heater-driven bubbling/vapour at 20 K. Lean temperature capability for this configuration is the single 20 K point (20000 mK), consistent with the NPL page. 'probe_arm' is used for the moving pull-rod/actuator since no tensile-specific enum exists.

equipment.description: Cryogen-free micro-manipulated probe stations for wafers up to 51 mm (2 in). CRX-VF adds a ±2.5 T vertical-field superconducting solenoid (10-420 K); CRX-4K is the lowest-temperature cryogen-free station (4.5 K base, 5-350 K, up to 675 K with the PS-HTSTAGE option). geometry.notes: Sources: Lake Shore CRX-4K specifications page (cache research/v5/cache/7e6f49fba2afae4a.txt) and Lake Shore Probe Stations catalog PDF probestationcatalog_l.pdf pp. 42-43 (cache research/v5/cache/75efd8eb8da79422.txt), whose cross-section diagram labels 'Radiation shield stage (35 K) / Sample stage (4.5 K) / Probe (15 K) / Probe arm base / Probe arm shield / Thermal anchors / Vacuum chamber base'. Scene geometry: a 280 mm OD x 140 mm tall nickel-plated aluminium vacuum chamber (229 mm top opening, 63.5 mm fused-quartz top viewport with 54.0 mm viewing area, NW40 pump port with isolation valve, NW25 gauge port, 0.25 in NPT gas port, 3.5 kPa relief valve) on an 800 x 670 mm platform; inside, a radiation shield with 132 mm lid and 50 mm IR-absorbing window surrounds the 4.5 K sample stage carrying a 31.8 mm grounded sample holder; two probe arms (this configuration; up to 6 with MMS-09 micromanipulators per catalog p.50) enter from the sides, arm anchored to the 35 K shield, probe anchored to the sample stage. Base temperature 4.5 K applies to 2 arms installed (5.5 K with 4, 6.0 K with 6). Cooldown 2 h, warmup 1.5 h, cycle 4 h, vibration at sample <1 um, base pressure <1e-5 Torr. Ring magnet kit (PS-RING-MAG-KIT) and PS-HTSTAGE (20-675 K) are options, not installed. Cryogen enum: the CCR runs from a 3-phase 6.6-7.8 kW water-cooled compressor, consistent with a GM cooler, but the datasheet never names the cooler type - treat cryogen_free_gm as unconfirmed.

geometry.notes: Lake Shore (Environment by Janis) CCS-400: optical, high-temperature (500 K), sample-in-vacuum, bottom-loading closed-cycle refrigerator cryostat, <4 K to 500 K with the 408 cold head (1 W at 4.2 K), typical stability +/-50 mK, cooldown 1.5 h to 3 h (CCS-400 column). Datasheet column mapping (CCS-100 / 300S / 300ST / 400 / 400H) was read from pdftotext layout: height 56-84 / 71-99 / 71-99 / 61-89 / 66-94 cm; weight 16-30 kg; window block 83-85 mm square for CCS-100 and CCS-400 (38 mm square for CCS-300S). The cold head is a required ordering choice (204, 204N, 101, 408, 415, 418); this scene assumes the 408 as the catalog file does. Lake Shore does not name the cold head maker; the '408 / 1 W at 4.2 K' spec matches the SHI RDK-408D2 two-stage GM cryocooler (557 x 180 x 294 mm, 18 kg, <3.5 K, first stage 40/50 W at 43 K), used here only for the first-stage temperature and flagged as an inference. Every cryostat ships with a Lake Shore temperature controller and calibrated sensor; sample wiring (WH-10P etc.) and windows are ordered separately, so dc/coax counts are 0 in this standard configuration. Moving parts: GM displacer in the cold head (rate not published), remote water-cooled helium compressor, external vacuum pump; no magnet, no VSM, no liquid cryogen. Sources: ccr-vacuum.pdf (code 102126), cryostat-feedthroughs product page, cryostatwindows.pdf, shicryogenics.com RDK-408D2 page.

geometry.notes: Vertical cryogen-free PPMS: a single Cryomech two-stage pulse tube sits in helium gas in a 'bucket' tank (not vacuum-mounted); first stage ~45 K cools the main and annulus radiation shields and cryopump stage 1; the second stage condenses He onto a ~150 cc LHe pool that cools the 4 K Plate by thermosiphon; the switch-less 14 T NbTi solenoid is conduction-cooled by solid contact to the 4 K Plate and produces a vertical (longitudinal) field at 120 A full field. The sample chamber (2.5 cm clear bore) runs down the magnet bore; 4.2 K helium from the bucket passes a counter-flow heat exchanger and mass-flow controller (0-5000 sccm) into the cooling annulus around the chamber and returns via the circulation scroll pump (5-50 Torr return, 500-800 Torr outlet), giving 1.8-400 K at the puck. The puck (2.3 cm Cu, Au plated) plugs into the 12-pin keyed connector at the chamber bottom; the block thermometer is clamped to the puck interface outside the chamber. Magnet centre 4.05 cm above puck surface; 14 T uniformity +/-0.1% over 5.5 cm on axis. Options modelled: ETO (2 channels), VSM (linear transport motor on the top KF flange, 6.3 mm coil bore, 9 mm coil separation, 40 Hz x 2 mm) and Heat Capacity (3 x 3 mm platform, puck microcalorimeter in high vacuum via the integrated cryopump). No optical windows in this configuration (magneto-optic FOSH option not installed). Outer dimensions are D x W x H for cryostat plus can rack; the 67x70x100 cm electronics cabinet and 69x50x62 cm compressor stand apart. 14 T startup 40 h typical; puck 300 K to 1.9 K in under 40 min.

Base temp 3.5-3.8 K per shroud page, 3.8-320 K per spec sheet; cooldown < 4.5 h to 5 K; cooling power > 170 mW @ 5 K; vibration < 5 nm p-p vertical. Pulse-tube identification and the 1 Hz valve rate come from Vadia et al., PRX Quantum 2, 040318 (2021) (arXiv:2103.05619, co-authored by attocube), which also reports '1 Hz periodic pattern of mechanical pulses characteristic of closed-cycle coolers'; attocube's own pages only call it a 'closed-cycle cryostat' with 'cryocooler assembly ... underneath'. geometry.notes: Scene: a bare single-stage Gifford-McMahon cold head, not a cryostat. Geometry from Cryomech drawing CH1A600 rev A (supersedes CH10600): 241.3 mm room-temperature flange; 267.7 mm motor housing with two eyebolts above the flange; 127 mm diameter cold cylinder 307.8 mm long below the flange ending in a bare copper heat exchanger (8x M10 on 101.6 mm BC). Two 3/4 inch Aeroquip helium couplings exit the side 57.2 mm above the flange, reaching 237.8 mm from the axis. Cold head weight 42 kg. Separate water-cooled CPA1114 compressor 61 x 61 x 79 cm, 191 kg, 440/480 VAC 3-phase 60 Hz, 12.5 kW, joined by two 3 m (10 ft) 1 inch ID flex lines (6.8 kg per pair) and a motor cord of the same length. Performance: 600 W at 80 K certified at 60 Hz, 510 W at 70 K, 350 W at 50 K, <=25 K no load, <1 h cooldown. The spec sheet's '430 W at 600 K' is a typo for the 60 K point. Animation: displacer reciprocates inside the cold cylinder at an unpublished GM rate; compressor hum at mains frequency; helium pulses in the flex lines. Sources: spec sheet (Oct 28 2024), product page, CH1A600 cold head drawing, AL600 CPA1114 system drawing rev E (snapshots research/v5/cache/4cbe6c75b1d7a4bb.txt, 6b7370d24a1c1775.txt, 03ec8b940f752b63.txt, 35bcf16c6a699f01.txt).

Geometry for the 3D model: an 813 mm wide, 1257 mm tall cylinder (liftover height 40 in / 1016 mm per the same sheet) with an offset 317 mm neck; inside, a 731 mm diameter cavity with a 52 L LN2 pool under a turn-tray and 676 mm of usable height above it filled by 12 square racks (12 shelves of 100-cell boxes) plus 4 mini racks, two Pt-1000 probes in a central three-tube sensor assembly. The catalog's primary document (bsilab, ML-CRYO0032 E, 2015) was used for consistency with the catalog values (370 L, 676 mm, 1257 mm); the current MVE sheet ML-000019 Rev 0 (https://mvebio.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2025/01/MVE-HEco-800-Series-Spec-Sheet-091024.pdf) gives 360 L w/o inventory, 673 mm usable height, 1350 mm overall (TS model), 1038 mm liftover, 218 kg empty / 526 kg full. Temperatures: -190 C top box = 83.15 K; LN2 pool assumed at its 77.3 K boiling point (the source states LN2, not a temperature).

geometry.notes: CG-400 = SPEX item 6875 (same 52x55x46 cm, 20 kg specs appear in the SPEX 14th Edition Handbook p.49 for the 6875). Single grinding chamber in the lid: a dual-electromagnet coil housing hangs into an insulated LN2 tub; the closed vial sits inside the coil, fully immersed, and the steel impactor is shuttled magnetically end-to-end at the programmed cps (the mill's only moving part; the user-facing 'rate' is back-and-forth cycles per second, so 10 cps = 20 impacts/s per the sibling 6770 manual, https://isolab.ess.washington.edu/resources/manuals/SPEX_Cryo_Mill.pdf). LN2 level sensor shuts the mill down when low; auto-fill (6875A/CG-450) is NOT fitted in this configuration. Touchscreen controller stores 20 programs, dual USB. No vacuum, no magnet spec, no sample electrical connections. Render: box cabinet with lid, LN2 pool at 77 K with boil-off vapour, one cylindrical vial in a coil with an oscillating impactor (8-15 Hz).

geometry.notes: Outer dimensions come from the dimension callouts on the Cryogenic m-CFMS flyer photo (page 1): the 900 mm arrow is vertical beside the cryostat, 440 mm runs across the front of the base, 660 mm along the side (verified by rendering the PDF page). Stage temperatures: the m-CFMS product page gives pulse tube base <3 K and VTI 1.6-400 K; the magnet is conduction-cooled by the same cryocooler (same page: 'Cooling for both the magnet and the sample space is provided by a cryocooler'), so it is modelled at the cryocooler stage temperature. The dc_twisted_pair wiring entry has count 0 because the brochure names twisted pairs as a wiring option but gives no count; the six-contact-per-socket figure (two sockets) is from the Resistivity and Hall Effect product page for the standard DC probe. Optical access (VTI-base) and He-3 insert are options NOT fitted in this configuration, hence windows count 0. The 25 mm VTI variant on the m-CFMS page quotes a '100 mm long isothermal region, with a possibility of a single optical access'; this configuration uses the 30 mm VTI so that length is not applied. Flyer-only numbers: Weight Approx. 1,455 lbs (660 kg); Floor load capacity of the chamber (Equally distributed load) 88 lbs (40 kg). Each zone rear wall carries a grid of round cable ports (flyer photo) for the user-supplied charge/discharge power supply; the ADBC-T itself has no instrumentation lines, so wiring kind is 'none'. Options not fitted in this configuration: pressure relief vent, gas detector, CO2 fire extinguisher, impedance measurement function, custom battery mounting boards, water-cooled refrigeration. geometry.notes: Compact ultra-low-temperature stirred-liquid metrology bath, -80 C to 100 C, cascade refrigeration with two 1/4 HP compressors and a 500 W heater; 1700 VA at 115 V/60 Hz or 230 V/50 Hz. Outer box 305 W x 762 H x 610 D mm, 52 kg, casters fitted. The 4 L stainless-steel tank sits under an insulated lid carrying the stirring motor (under a motor cover), the control PRT in a small hole, and the 83 x 114 mm rectangular access hole with an insulated access cover the user may drill for probe fixtures; max immersion 180 mm. Fluid level 12 to 50 mm below tank top. Back panel: circuit breaker, IEC power inlet, drain valve, RS-232 connector, removable vent panel. Stability +/-0.006 C and uniformity +/-0.008 C at -80 C (ethanol); cooling 25 C to -80 C in 130 min. geometry.notes: Sources: Lake Shore FWPX technical-specifications page (cache research/v5/cache/9ae700052f15978d.txt) and Lake Shore Probe Stations catalog PDF probestationcatalog_l.pdf pp. 38-39 (cache research/v5/cache/75efd8eb8da79422.txt), whose cross-section diagram labels 'Radiation shield stage (20 K) / Sample stage (4.5 K) / Probe (25 K) / Probe arm base / Probe arm shield / Thermal anchors / Vacuum chamber base'. Scene geometry: a 406 mm OD x 178 mm tall nickel-plated aluminium vacuum chamber (330 mm top opening, 102 mm fused-quartz top viewport with 91 mm viewing area, NW40 pump port with isolation valve, NW25 gauge port, 0.25 in NPT gas port, 3.5 kPa relief valve) on a 1067 x 851 mm platform; inside, a nickel-plated aluminium radiation shield with 180 mm lid and 159 mm IR-absorbing window (152 mm viewing area) surrounds the 4.5 K x-y translating sample stage carrying a 102 mm grounded SH-4.00-G sample holder; six micromanipulated probe arms enter from the sides, arm anchored to the 20 K shield, probe anchored to the sample stage. Cooling is a 2-stage continuous-flow cryostat (sample + radiation shield) fed by a large-bore S-style LHe/LN2 transfer line with 12.7 mm top-port Dewar withdrawal; no compressor or cold head, so the only mechanical motion is cryogen flow, the pump, and operator-driven stage/probe moves. Base 4.5 K with up to 6 arms (3.5 K with PS-LT, not fitted); control range 5-475 K on the current web page (4.5-420 K in the catalog PDF); cooldown 1.5 h, warmup 1.5 h, cycle 3.5 h, vibration <30 nm, base pressure <1e-5 Torr, no magnet option, no backside optical access. geometry.notes: Standard LTS420 (non-E) with T96-S controller and LNP96-S LN2 pump. Geometry: a flat 166 x 90 x 24 mm stage body (Linkam spec page; McCrone lists an older '160 x 80 x 24 mm') carrying a 53.5 x 43 mm silver block; swing-out lid with a standard 18 mm viewing aperture (Bioimager, Linkam distributor; 35/50 mm on request); inner lid for stability. Window count 2 = top lid window plus a lower window inferred only from 'Can be used with transmitted or reflected light' and the published condenser working distance of 12.5 mm; the lower aperture size is not published. Stage body is water-cooled for work above 300 C (brochure). Objective min working distance 6.5 mm, condenser 12.5 mm. Temperature < -195 C (78 K) to 420 C, stability < 0.01 C, rates 0.01-50 C/min. LN2 is pumped from the LNP96 dewar by the control unit's pumps (T96-controlled) and injected directly into the block; the T96 drives the Pt100 sensor and heater. No electrical sample lines in this configuration (LTS420E variants add 2-pin LEMO/BNC/probes). geometry.notes: Scene source: MI 6800C brochure (2021, 8 pp.) and the mintl.com product page, which repeats the brochure text; no third-party facility paper naming the 6800C was found, and MI does not publish cryostat footprint, height or weight. Configuration CFMS-9T-30-H3: 9 T vertical-field cryogen-free magnet (52 mm bore, 0.02 % over 1 cm3, 120 A / 5 V supply), 30 mm VTI with JT-condensed 4He gas loop and external scroll pump to 1.3 K, two-stage pulse-tube cryocooler (35 W @ 45 K / 0.9 W @ 4.2 K, F70 water-cooled compressor, 30,000-40,000 h service), top-loading airlock + gate valve, dual TO-8 probe with 8 PTFE-insulated silver wires per socket (16 sample lines total). No optical windows: the sample is enclosed in a VTI accessed only via airlock. 3He insert (22 mm OD, < 300 mK) and 14 T / 40 mm VTI are options not in this configuration. Rendering guidance: draw a vertical cylinder with top-mounted airlock/gate valve and probe, a separate 444 x 529 x 576 mm compressor box, and the 6020Q bridge rack; treat the outer-can dimensions as unknown.

geometry.notes: Single source: 800 Series Cryostream Operating and Instruction Guide, Oxford Cryosystems 2014 (SFU mirror), text cached at research/v5/cache/4dfb8bc9e86001d6.txt (65 pages). Cryostream Plus differs from the standard only by its 500 K upper limit (Section 5.1); all geometry is identical. Physical layout from the manual: coldhead with integral vacuum-insulated transfer line (1500 mm flexible + 905 mm rigid leg, min bend radius 200 mm, ~900 mm leg uses top 850 mm of dewar) plunged into the unpressurised 60 L ES60 dewar (NW50 KF neck, 50 mm bore); coldhead clamped in the Varibeam stand with fine X/Y/Z translation; red 6 mm PTFE dry-air tube to the coldhead; 3.5 m Coldhead Cable to the controller (placed < 3 m from coldhead, < 2 m from the gas pump). Vacuum space re-pumped every 12-18 months via the pump-out adaptor (NW16/KF16) with the CRH25 re-activation heater. Nothing moves in the coldhead itself: the only motion is the N2 gas flow driven by the separate gas pump, the dry-air shroud, and LN2 consumption/boil-off from the dewar. 'outer' uses the Varibeam stand envelope (600 mm height, 430 mm reach) because the coldhead body has no published dimensions. Tavily quota was exhausted; corpora.tika.apache.org (older manual with 'How the Cryostream Cooler Works') and the APS 700 quick-start PDF were unreachable (DNS / 403).

geometry.notes: Compact tabletop LN2 bath optical cryostat, 175 x 175 x 450 mm, 5 kg (manual Table 3-5 and 7.3). Top: LN2 fill/vent pipe, nitrogen exhaust flow needle valve, two 10-pin connectors (diagnostic, experimental) on the OVC top plate, DN16NW OVC evacuation port with pressure-relief plates. Inside: 1.2 L LN2 reservoir around a central heat-exchanger support tube; capillary feeds a gravity-fed heat exchanger carrying heater + PT100; sample holder (20 x 50 mm) bolts beneath, sample in vacuum ('No cold windows', no radiation-shield windows). Four radial Spectrosil WF windows + one axial blank, each held by four nylon screws and an O-ring, 35 mm clear aperture, f/1 (QD Oxford page: 'Large illumination area: 35 mm diameter window aperture'; 'Weight: 5 kg'). Charcoal sorb with 150 ohm heater on the reservoir keeps the OVC below 1e-4 mbar. 77.2-500 K, +/-0.1 K, cooldown 20 min, hold >= 15 h. No cryocooler, no magnet; only motion is LN2 boil-off vapour at the vent and the optional external pump. Sources: QD Oxford Optistat matrix PDF (OPTSS 0926 R5, cache c73e273061693731), QD Oxford product page https://www.qd-oxford.com/products/optistat_spectroscopy.html (cache 295cbbaf14723ca3), Oxford Instruments Optistat family brochure (cache d52046bdb551703d), Oxford Instruments Optistat DN-V Operators Manual Issue 2.0 Dec 2020 (andor.oxinst.com robots.txt disallows the snapshot script; PDF fetched via WebFetch and text extracted locally with pypdf into the session scratchpad).

geometry.notes: Scene: vertical aluminium OVC of stacked cylindrical sections on a cross-braced steel frame; inside, top plate -> PT1 (77 K) -> PT2 (4 K copper shield, magnet hangs from it) -> still (700 mK shield) -> cold plate (100 mK) -> 360 mm mixing chamber plate (< 10 mK; MX450 guaranteed > 450 uW at 100 mK, > 12 uW at 20 mK). One Sumitomo RP-182B2S pulse tube (PTR options 1.35/1.50/1.80 W; 1.5 W = RP-182B2S) with separated valve unit. One 117 x 252 mm Secondary Insert slot carries the BLL-72 bottom-loader SI with cold finger: 28 SMA hermetic + 4 x 24-way Fischer at room temperature, 28 SMP + 2 x 51-way Nano-D at the cold finger, plus one spare ISO100 LOS port (up to 37 coax). The 72 mm x 144 mm puck enters from below through a vacuum lock on a removable loading arm; load < 15 min, 10 h cooldown, < 12 mK and 150 uW at 100 mK at the puck. 14 T solenoid, quench protected, ramps to full field in 1 h or less; patented gas-gap heat switches with a remote sorb (outgassed at ~30 K) link the plates. Also 2 x KF40 + 2 x KF25 LOS ports on the top plate. CAVEATS: PT1/PT2/still/cold-plate temperatures and the 2 m x 0.6 m outer size come from the published Sheffield QSHS Proteox MX500 (8 T custom magnet), the closest documented Proteox MX, not an MX450 datasheet. The catalog unknown stands: the 14 T + 72 mm / 28-coax pairing is 'Dependent on magnet selection' and undocumented; the BLL-60 (77 mm bore, 22 coax, 96 DC) may be the actual 14 T puck. A Pisa MX450 (no magnet) is wired with 7 coax, 2 x 24-wire DC looms and 2 single-mode fibres (cisup.unipi.it/?p=5370), a different real-world wiring.

geometry.notes: Scene: vertical aluminium OVC of stacked cylindrical sections on a cross-braced steel frame; inside, top plate -> PT1 (77 K) -> PT2 (4 K copper shield, magnet hangs from it) -> still (700 mK shield) -> cold plate (100 mK) -> 360 mm mixing chamber plate (< 10 mK; MX450 guaranteed > 450 uW at 100 mK, > 12 uW at 20 mK). One Sumitomo RP-182B2S pulse tube (PTR options 1.35/1.50/1.80 W; 1.5 W = RP-182B2S) with separated valve unit. One 117 x 252 mm Secondary Insert slot carries the BLL-72 bottom-loader SI with cold finger: 28 SMA hermetic + 4 x 24-way Fischer at room temperature, 28 SMP + 2 x 51-way Nano-D at the cold finger, plus one spare ISO100 LOS port (up to 37 coax). The 72 mm x 144 mm puck enters from below through a vacuum lock on a removable loading arm; load < 15 min, 10 h cooldown, < 12 mK and 150 uW at 100 mK at the puck. 14 T solenoid, quench protected, ramps to full field in 1 h or less; patented gas-gap heat switches with a remote sorb (outgassed at ~30 K) link the plates. Also 2 x KF40 + 2 x KF25 LOS ports on the top plate. CAVEATS: PT1/PT2/still/cold-plate temperatures and the 2 m x 0.6 m outer size come from the published Sheffield QSHS Proteox MX500 (8 T custom magnet), the closest documented Proteox MX, not an MX450 datasheet. The catalog unknown stands: the 14 T + 72 mm / 28-coax pairing is 'Dependent on magnet selection' and undocumented; the BLL-60 (77 mm bore, 22 coax, 96 DC) may be the actual 14 T puck. A Pisa MX450 (no magnet) is wired with 7 coax, 2 x 24-wire DC looms and 2 single-mode fibres (cisup.unipi.it/?p=5370), a different real-world wiring.

bio_cryo_fluorescence_vitrified.plain_name: Examine a sample under the microscope while keeping it cold

reported_conditions.as_printed: − 183 °C (liquid ethane); Leica EM GP at 12 °C, 50% humidity
all tools fully cooled to liquid nitrogen temperatures

requirements.rationale: Last et al. (2023) state that devitrification occurs when vitrified samples are heated above approximately 136 K; Huebinger & Bastiaens (2026) state that heating above the glass transition devitrifies the sample. Staying below this temperature is therefore a stated physical necessity for vitrified specimens, not merely the papers' choice. The sources themselves hold the stage at 77 K.
Fluorescence imaging of the cold specimen requires an optical path to the sample; Last et al. image through a 0.9 NA air objective on a Linkam CMS196v3 cryo-stage.

Condensation/frost: a cold specimen or window below the frost point collects ice unless the sample space is evacuated or purged with dry gas (pm_015, pm_016). Applies only when the operating temperature is at or below 0 °C.

sources.citation: Last, M. G. F., Tuijtel, M. W., Voortman, L. M., Sharp, T. H. (2023). Selecting optimal support grids for super-resolution cryogenic correlated light and electron microscopy. Scientific Reports 13, 8270.

Berkamp, S., Daviran, D., Smeets, M., Caignard, A., Jani, R. A., Sundermeyer, P., Jonker, C., Gerlach, S., Hoffmann, B., Lau, K., Sachse, C. (2023). Correlative Light and Electron Cryo-Microscopy Workflow Combining Micropatterning, Ice Shield, and an In-Chamber Fluorescence Light Microscope. Bio-protocol 13(24), e4901.
Huebinger, J., Bastiaens, P. I. H. (2026). Determination of factors that allow cryogenic nanoscopy with high power illumination without devitrification. PLoS One 21(3), e0344631.

evidence.applies_to: Moist air in contact with any surface colder than the dew point (e.g. cold sample or window)
evidence.claim: Air cannot be cooled below its dew point without water vapour condensing out of the air; when dew points are below 0 °C, freezing temperatures are a greater possibility.
evidence.document_title: 13.6 Humidity, Evaporation, and Boiling - College Physics 2e | OpenStax
evidence.location: Section 13.6, discussion after Example 'Calculating Humidity and Dew Point'
evidence.quote: The importance of dew point is that air temperature cannot drop below 10.0ºC in part (b), or –10.0ºC in part (c), without water vapor condensing out of the air. [...] When dew points are below 0ºC, freezing temperatures are a greater possibility, which explains why farmers keep track of the dew point.
evidence.verification: corrected after check: quote re-fetched and normalised to page text (removed spaced/duplicated math symbols) and extended with the source's 'When dew points are below 0ºC...' sentence; claim's second clause reworded from 'freezing (frost) becomes likely' to the source's 'freezing temperatures are a greater possibility' (air temperature, not surface frost)

evidence.applies_to: Cryogenic optical microscopy stages (sample below ~135 K) in vacuum or nitrogen purge
evidence.claim: A cryostage keeps condensable gases away from the cold specimen by pulling a vacuum or using a dry gas purge; even so, trace water vapour can still deposit as frost.
evidence.document_title: Reducing Frost during Cryoimaging Using a Hygroscopic Ice Frame
evidence.quote: A cryostage maintains an environment devoid of water vapor and condensable gases by either pulling a vacuum or using a dry gas purge. However, despite the dry environment, trace levels of condensable water vapor can still accumulate on the sample as frost.

requirements.rationale: Park et al. (2026) cooled to −140 °C, the lowest point of that paper's freezing/melting cycles; this is the paper's choice set by the phase behaviour studied, and the user confirms −140 °C as the required operating point.
Raman scattering is collected through the stage window with a microscope objective in both sources; optical access to the cold sample is intrinsic to the technique.

Park et al. (2026) and Pamula et al. (2025) load the sample in a 15 mm diameter quartz crucible inside the stage, so the stage must accept a 15 mm sample; this is the papers' sample format, confirmed by the user.

Pamula et al. (2025) focus through the stage with a 6.5 mm working-distance objective. The working distance that the stage window geometry requires must not exceed the objective's 6.5 mm, so a stage requiring more than 6.5 mm would be incompatible with this optical setup. Non-mandatory because a longer-WD objective could be substituted.

Condensation/frost: a cold specimen or window below the frost point collects ice unless the sample space is evacuated or purged with dry gas (pm_015, pm_016). Applies only when the operating temperature is at or below 0 °C.

Excitation and emission pass through cryostat windows (borosilicate in Swidinsky et al.; quartz in Shyam et al.); optical access is intrinsic to photoluminescence in a cryostat.
Swidinsky et al. (2024) used 25 × 25 × 2 mm fused silica substrates mounted on the coldfinger; the cryostat must accept a 25 mm wide sample. Sample size is this paper's choice, confirmed by the user.
Swidinsky et al. (2024) used 25 × 25 × 2 mm fused silica substrates; the cryostat must accept a 25 mm long sample. This paper's choice, confirmed by the user.
Both papers evacuate the sample space before cooling (Swidinsky et al. below 1e-6 mbar; Shyam et al. 1e-5 mbar); an evacuable sample space is required.
Swidinsky et al. (2024) held the sample below 1e-6 mbar (100 uPa). Non-mandatory: Shyam et al. (2026) worked at 1e-5 mbar, so the exact vacuum level is a per-paper choice.

requirements.rationale: Tuokkola et al. (2025) operate at ~10 mK and Place et al. (2021) at a ~9–20 mK base; 20 mK is the upper end of what these papers used. Neither source states a minimum temperature as a physical necessity, so this is the papers' operating range confirmed by the user.

Observed frequencies in the sources reach 6.23 GHz (Tuokkola et al. readout resonators) and 7.3 GHz (Place et al. readout resonators); the 8 GHz figure adds margin above these and is the profile author's choice (user_entered), see reported_conditions for the observed values.

Both papers enclose the sample in high-permeability magnetic shielding (Amumetal shield and QCage shielding in Tuokkola et al.; mu-metal can in Place et al., stated to reduce ambient-field penetration during the superconducting transition). User confirms shielding is required.

Neither paper states the number of coaxial lines. At least one input (drive/readout) and one output (readout) line are implied by the described signal path, so 2 is an inferred lower bound. Non-mandatory.
Place et al. (2021) dice chips into 7 × 7 mm squares; the sample holder must accept a 7 mm wide chip. Chip size is this paper's design choice, confirmed by the user.
Place et al. (2021) dice chips into 7 × 7 mm squares; the sample holder must accept a 7 mm long chip. This paper's design choice, confirmed by the user.

requirements.rationale: The Coupling-LNAs must operate at a physical temperature of 15 K.
The dewar reaches a vacuum of 1e-5 Pa to suppress gas conduction and convection to the cold parts.
The OMT and LNAs sit inside a vacuum dewar.
The sky signal enters the dewar through a large film vacuum window in front of the OMT.
The 728.3 mm long OMT must fit inside the cold space.
The OMT has a 189 mm internal receiving aperture (its outer envelope is larger), which sets the minimum clear diameter.

chem_cryo_ion_ir_spectroscopy.confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
chem_cryo_ion_ir_spectroscopy.description: Mass- and mobility-selected ions are stored in a cryogenic ion trap held between 30 and 45 K by a closed-cycle helium cryostat, where a pulsed 20% N2/80% He gas mixture forms weakly bound messenger-tagged complexes at about 2e-6 mbar; a tunable mid-IR source is stepped in 2 cm-1 steps from 990 to 1810 cm-1 and tag loss gives a diagnostic vibrational fingerprint. This is how isomeric small molecules, glycans and drug metabolites are distinguished when mass spectrometry alone cannot.
keywords: Identify a molecule by chilling its ions and shining infrared on them
chem_cryo_ion_ir_spectroscopy.name: Cryogenic messenger-tagging infrared ion spectroscopy in a 30-45 K trap at 2e-6 mbar
chem_cryo_ion_ir_spectroscopy.plain_name: Identify a molecule by chilling its ions and shining infrared on them

requirements.rationale: The trap is operated between 30 and 45 K, tuned for the analyte; outside that window the messenger tag either does not bind or does not detach cleanly.
Tagging requires the trap to be able to reach 30 K; a machine with a higher base temperature cannot condense the N2 messenger onto the ions.
The ions are stored in an evacuated trap chamber; the experiment is impossible in an atmospheric-pressure cold space.
Typical operation is at about 2e-6 mbar inside the trap chamber, so the machine must pump at least that low with the tagging gas pulsed in.
The tunable mid-IR beam has to enter the cold trap and overlap the stored ion cloud, which requires an optical window into the cold space.
Optional: the trap is cooled by a closed-cycle helium cryostat with a single-stage coldhead, so no liquid cryogen is consumed; a bath-cooled implementation would also reach the required temperature.

chem_cryomilling_amorphization.description: Crystalline bosentan is milled in a stainless-steel grinding vessel immersed in liquid nitrogen in a Retsch CryoMill at an impact frequency of 9 cycles per second for a total of 2.5 h, converting it to the amorphous state without the thermal degradation that ambient milling or melt-quenching would cause. The amorphous product is then compared with the melt-quenched glass.
keywords: Grind a medicine into powder while liquid nitrogen keeps it brittle
chem_cryomilling_amorphization.name: Cryogenic impact milling of a crystalline drug under liquid nitrogen for 2.5 h at 9 impacts per second to produce the amorphous form
chem_cryomilling_amorphization.plain_name: Grind a medicine into powder while liquid nitrogen keeps it brittle
reported_equipment: CryoMill ~100-240 V-50/60 Hz, Retsch GmbH, Germany

requirements.rationale: The grinding jar is held at liquid-nitrogen temperature (-196 C = 77150 mK) throughout, which is what embrittles the drug and stops it recrystallising or degrading during milling.
The procedure consumes liquid nitrogen: the milling vessel is physically immersed in it, so a purely mechanical or electrically cooled machine cannot reproduce the process.
The machine has to be a cryogenic impact mill: the amorphisation comes from mechanical impact delivered while the sample is at cryogenic temperature.
Milling was carried out at 9 impacts per second (9 Hz), which must lie inside the mill's selectable frequency range.
Full amorphisation needed 2.5 h (9000 s) of milling, so the machine's programmable grinding time (with intermediate cooling cycles) must reach that total.

chem_epr_frozen_catalyst.description: Chromium-doped silicoaluminophosphate molecular sieves are characterised by continuous-wave X-band EPR (about 9.5 GHz) with the sample cell in a liquid-nitrogen finger dewar at 77 K, and by Q-band (about 33.8 GHz) pulsed HYSCORE at 1224.1 mT and 40 K, to locate the chromium site and its coordination. Freezing the sample is what narrows the lines and makes the hyperfine couplings resolvable.
keywords: Detect unpaired electrons in a deep-frozen catalyst sample
chem_epr_frozen_catalyst.name: Frozen-sample EPR of a transition-metal catalyst: X-band CW at 77 K in a liquid-nitrogen finger dewar and Q-band pulsed HYSCORE at 40 K and 1224.1 mT

reported_equipment: Bruker EMX EPR spectrometer equipped with a super-high-Q cavity
finger Dewar filled with liquid nitrogen

requirements.rationale: The study needs both the 77 K continuous-wave measurement and the 40 K pulsed measurement, so the sample space must cover 40-77 K.
The pulsed HYSCORE experiments are run at 40 K, which a liquid-nitrogen bath alone cannot reach; the machine must get to 40 K or below.
The Q-band pulsed measurements are made at a field of 1224.1 mT, so the magnet around the cold sample must reach at least that field.
Optional: the 77 K part of the work is done by immersing the EPR cell in a liquid-nitrogen finger dewar; a closed-cycle variable-temperature insert could reach 77 K without liquid nitrogen.
Microwaves from X-band (about 9.5 GHz) to Q-band (about 33.8 GHz) must be delivered to the cold sample for the combined CW and pulsed measurements.

chem_lyophilization_cycle.description: A nucleic-acid lipid-nanoparticle drug product is frozen on the shelves at -50 C, primary-dried at a shelf temperature of -10 C under 180 mTorr chamber pressure and secondary-dried at 40 C (optimised variant: -15 C primary, 30 C secondary) in a pilot freeze dryer, with the sublimed water captured on the ice condenser. This is the standard cycle structure for parenteral lyophilised drug products.
keywords: Freeze-dry a medicine into a shelf-stable powder
chem_lyophilization_cycle.name: Pharmaceutical lyophilization cycle in vials: freezing at -50 C, primary drying at -10 C and 180 mTorr, secondary drying at 40 C
chem_lyophilization_cycle.plain_name: Freeze-dry a medicine into a shelf-stable powder
reported_equipment: Virtis Genesis Pilot Freeze Dryer (SP, Warminster, PA, USA)

requirements.rationale: The shelves must span the whole recipe, from the -50 C freezing step to the 40 C secondary-drying step.
Freezing is done on the shelves at -50 C; a dryer whose shelves cannot reach -50 C cannot execute this freezing step.
Primary drying is sublimation under vacuum; without an evacuated product chamber there is no lyophilisation.
Primary drying runs at 180 mTorr (0.18 Torr) chamber pressure, so the dryer must pump at least that low.
The procedure is a freeze-drying cycle: the machine must be a lyophiliser with controllable shelves and an ice condenser, not merely a cold evacuated space.

Optional: pharmaceutical primary drying is almost always controlled between 50 and 200 mTorr, so a dryer must be able to hold a set pressure inside that window rather than only pump to its ultimate vacuum.

chem_matrix_isolation_ir.confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
chem_matrix_isolation_ir.description: A heterocyclic compound is sublimed and co-deposited with a large excess of argon onto a CsI window held at 15 K inside a closed-cycle helium cryostat evacuated to about 3.5e-5 mbar; mid-IR spectra (4000-400 cm-1) are recorded on the isolated monomers and followed through broadband UV irradiation from a 500 W Hg(Xe) lamp. This is the standard matrix-isolation route to conformers, photoproducts and reactive intermediates in chemistry.
keywords: Trap single molecules in frozen argon and study them with infrared light
chem_matrix_isolation_ir.name: Matrix-isolation FTIR spectroscopy of a sublimed heterocycle in solid argon at 15 K with broadband UV photolysis

reported_equipment: closed-cycle helium cryostat with a DE-202 A expander

requirements.rationale: The matrix is deposited and held with the optical substrate at 15 K; the machine must be able to reach and hold that sample temperature.
Argon matrix isolation needs a base temperature of 15 K or lower; a machine whose lowest temperature is above 15 K cannot form a rigid Ar matrix.
Deposition and spectroscopy happen inside an evacuated chamber; an atmospheric-pressure cold space would frost the window and destroy the matrix.
The reported working vacuum of the matrix chamber is about 3.5e-5 mbar; poorer vacuum deposits residual water and air with the matrix gas.
The IR beam and the UV photolysis beam must reach the cold deposit, so the cold space needs optical windows; the sample itself sits on a cold optical substrate.
Spectra are taken over 4000-400 cm-1, i.e. 2500-25000 nm, so the cryostat windows must transmit the whole mid-infrared (hence CsI rather than glass or quartz).

chem_mdsc_frozen_tg.description: A liquid vaccine formulation is sealed in a hermetic Tzero pan, equilibrated at -70 C, held for 5 minutes and ramped at 1 C/min to 100 C with heat-cool temperature modulation, so that the glass transition of the maximally freeze-concentrated solution can be read from the reversing heat-flow signal. That transition sets the maximum allowable product temperature of the subsequent freeze-drying cycle.
keywords: Find the temperature at which a frozen medicine mixture softens

requirements.rationale: The measurement cycle runs from an equilibration at -70 C up to 100 C in one ramp, so the sample space must cover that whole span.
The glass transition of the freeze-concentrate is below -30 C, so the instrument must equilibrate at -70 C before the ramp begins.
The underlying heating ramp is 1 C/min (1000 mK/min); the machine must be able to drive at least that rate under control.
The readout is a modulated differential-scanning-calorimetry heat-flow signal, so the machine must be a DSC and not just a cold stage.

The cold side must reach the Method 502.7 Cold (C2) ambient extreme of -46 C (227.15 K), which Method 503.7 says to select from the 502.7 tables for cold-region ground transfer.
The heated-enclosure condition carries 30-50 % RH; humidity control is optional for the shock itself.

env_ice_core_co2_sublimation_extraction.description: A 30 g ice cylinder (3.2 cm diameter, 4.5 cm long) is held at about -34 C in an evacuated glass sublimation vessel and sublimated by infrared halogen lamps; water is removed in traps down to -150 C, CO2/N2O are frozen in a liquid-nitrogen trap and sealed in a glass capillary for GC-IRMS, reconstructing past atmospheric CO2 and its carbon isotopes.
keywords: Release ancient air from ice-core pieces to measure past CO2
env_ice_core_co2_sublimation_extraction.name: Vacuum sublimation extraction of air from ice-core samples for d13CO2, CO2 and N2O (-34 C vessel, -150 C water trap, LN2 CO2 trap, <2e-7 mbar)

reported_equipment: Leybold turbo molecular pump backed by a rotary vane vacuum pump
Caburn CF sublimation vessel (33 mm o.d., 121 mm length)

requirements.rationale: The ice sample is held near -34 C (239.15 K) during sublimation, keeping it well below -20 C.
The external water trap must reach -150 C (123.15 K) to reach the required H2O vapour pressure.
Extraction is done in a high-vacuum sublimation line.
A leak-free line reaches below 2e-7 mbar on the high-vacuum side before sampling.
CO2 and N2O are frozen out in a trap immersed in liquid nitrogen.
The ice is trimmed to a 3.2 cm cylinder to fit the 3.3 cm vessel.
The ice piece is 4.5 cm long along the vessel axis.
The ice is sublimated by infrared light from halogen bulbs shining through the glass vessel.

geometry.notes: Six nested vessels: 300 K, 40 K, 4 K, Still (~0.8-0.9 K), HEX (~50 mK), MC (~10 mK). Vessel (shield) heights/diameters, Table II of arXiv:1904.05745: 300 K 1603x2620 mm; 40 K 1503x2765 mm; 4 K 1363x2471 mm; Still 1110x1850 mm; HEX 1020x1650 mm; MC 940x1365 mm. Inner Lead Shield (Roman lead, 1157 mm diam x 1568 mm, 60 mm thick, 3920 kg) between 4 K and Still; Top Lead (900 mm diam x 300 mm, 2110 kg) below MC plate above TSP. Cooling: five Cryomech PT415-RM (32 W at 45 K, 1.2 W at 4.2 K nominal each) on 40 K/4 K plates plus a custom dilution unit (~3-6 uW at 10 mK; 2 mW at 100 mK). 300 K plate suspended from a 4.7 m x 4.1 m steel I-beam Main Support Plate; total cold mass >15 t (LNGS page). Plate-to-plate distances Table I: 300K-40K 195 mm, 300K-4K 198 mm, 300K-Still 287 mm, Still-HEX 112 mm, HEX-MC 202 mm. Catalog file lists only the LNGS page; detailed numbers come from the collaboration's cryostat paper (Alduino et al., Cryogenics 2019, arXiv:1904.05745), first-results PRL (arXiv:1710.07988) and the PT noise-cancellation paper (arXiv:1712.02753). geometry.notes: Cryostat-100 is a vertical cylindrical LN2 boil-off calorimeter, not a sample cryostat: the 'stages' are the LN2-filled cold mass (78 K cold boundary) and the 293 K heater sleeve warm boundary; the 'sample' is an annular insulation shell wrapped around the cold mass. Published dimensions cover only the cold mass (167/168 mm diameter, 1 m / 1026 mm with guards; test-chamber effective length 575 mm per patent: 'using an effective length of the cold mass of 575 mm, the mean surface area for heat transfer through a typical 25-mm thick insulation test article is 0.35 m 2'). The vacuum canister's outer size is not published anywhere found, so the outer block carries cold-mass numbers with that stated; the canister must be modelled as a slightly larger stainless cylinder with a domed lid without quoting a dimension. Vacuum range: below 1x10-5 torr to 760 torr (NTRS 20150011030). Cold mass suspended by six Kevlar threads ('six KEVLAR threads with hooks and hardware for attachment and length adjustment', patent); CO2-filled vapor-pocket disks separate guard and test vessels; bake-out heaters on the canister exterior. Sources: KSC-TOPS-79 (cache 8a6b708eed0b8339), NTRS 20150011030 (c582e9d07eb670ef), NTRS 20100005254 tech brief (a6e9f3182a5f41ae), NTRS 20130012853 bulk-fill paper (3340971823e78180), US 8,628,238 B2 (2db63b0b75f42b79).

geometry.notes: Sources: Lake Shore CRX-4K specifications page (cache research/v5/cache/7e6f49fba2afae4a.txt) and Lake Shore Probe Stations catalog PDF probestationcatalog_l.pdf pp. 42-43 (cache research/v5/cache/75efd8eb8da79422.txt), whose cross-section diagram labels 'Radiation shield stage (35 K) / Sample stage (4.5 K) / Probe (15 K) / Probe arm base / Probe arm shield / Thermal anchors / Vacuum chamber base'. Scene geometry: a 280 mm OD x 140 mm tall nickel-plated aluminium vacuum chamber (229 mm top opening, 63.5 mm fused-quartz top viewport with 54.0 mm viewing area, NW40 pump port with isolation valve, NW25 gauge port, 0.25 in NPT gas port, 3.5 kPa relief valve) on an 800 x 670 mm platform; inside, a radiation shield with 132 mm lid and 50 mm IR-absorbing window surrounds the 4.5 K sample stage carrying a 31.8 mm grounded sample holder; two probe arms (this configuration; up to 6 with MMS-09 micromanipulators per catalog p.50) enter from the sides, arm anchored to the 35 K shield, probe anchored to the sample stage. Base temperature 4.5 K applies to 2 arms installed (5.5 K with 4, 6.0 K with 6). Cooldown 2 h, warmup 1.5 h, cycle 4 h, vibration at sample <1 um, base pressure <1e-5 Torr. Ring magnet kit (PS-RING-MAG-KIT) and PS-HTSTAGE (20-675 K) are options, not installed. Cryogen enum: the CCR runs from a 3-phase 6.6-7.8 kW water-cooled compressor, consistent with a GM cooler, but the datasheet never names the cooler type - treat cryogen_free_gm as unconfirmed.

evidence.review_status: independently re-fetched and verified by a second agent: Re-fetched the spec page with Tavily and as raw HTML. The Temperature range row has five separate cells with no colspan, under the header CCS-100/300S/300ST/400/400H. It reads '<4 K to 325 K' for CCS-100 and CCS-300S and '<4 K to 500 K' for CCS-400. I also read datasheet p.2 in memory with PyMuPDF (word coordinates plus cell rectangles). One merged cell (x 111-390, rows 101/408/415/418) reads '<4 K' for CCS-100/300S/300ST. The CCS-400 cell for rows 408/415/418 reads '<4 K' (its 101 row reads '<5 K'). So the assumed 408 head reaches <4 K on all three models, and 4000 mK is a conservative min bound.

geometry.notes: Lake Shore (Environment by Janis) CCS-400: optical, high-temperature (500 K), sample-in-vacuum, bottom-loading closed-cycle refrigerator cryostat, <4 K to 500 K with the 408 cold head (1 W at 4.2 K), typical stability +/-50 mK, cooldown 1.5 h to 3 h (CCS-400 column). Datasheet column mapping (CCS-100 / 300S / 300ST / 400 / 400H) was read from pdftotext layout: height 56-84 / 71-99 / 71-99 / 61-89 / 66-94 cm; weight 16-30 kg; window block 83-85 mm square for CCS-100 and CCS-400 (38 mm square for CCS-300S). The cold head is a required ordering choice (204, 204N, 101, 408, 415, 418); this scene assumes the 408 as the catalog file does. Lake Shore does not name the cold head maker; the '408 / 1 W at 4.2 K' spec matches the SHI RDK-408D2 two-stage GM cryocooler (557 x 180 x 294 mm, 18 kg, <3.5 K, first stage 40/50 W at 43 K), used here only for the first-stage temperature and flagged as an inference. Every cryostat ships with a Lake Shore temperature controller and calibrated sensor; sample wiring (WH-10P etc.) and windows are ordered separately, so dc/coax counts are 0 in this standard configuration. Moving parts: GM displacer in the cold head (rate not published), remote water-cooled helium compressor, external vacuum pump; no magnet, no VSM, no liquid cryogen. Sources: ccr-vacuum.pdf (code 102126), cryostat-feedthroughs product page, cryostatwindows.pdf, shicryogenics.com RDK-408D2 page.

The IFU's only 'vacuum' is the optional section-waste vacuum extractor (suction nozzle, adjustable intensity); the cryochamber is an atmospheric cabinet closed by a heated sliding window the operator opens to work, and the complete Technical Data give no chamber vacuum specification. module.vacuum_system (section-waste extraction) must not be read as vacuum.available.

The troubleshooting entry 'Sliding window collects condensation: Air humidity and room temperature too high' (p. 63) and sections brushed onto slides inside the chamber (p. 59) also show an atmospheric chamber. Keep module.vacuum_system separate.

Objective working distance 4.8 mm; v1.1 datasheet: lid window to element 4.5 mm, condenser (base window) distance 12.5 mm, light aperture 2.4 mm, lid window 0.17 mm - older values superseded by current page (4.8 mm, 2.0 mm, 0.5 mm). Window count 2 = lid window (current specs) + base plate window for transmitted light ('isolated from the sample by the stage base plate window', v1.1 datasheet); both on the vertical optical axis. Quick-release gas valves for atmospheric control. Stage is static apart from manual XY manipulators, pumped LN2/nitrogen gas flow through the block, and optional water circulation; no pulse tube, no magnet. Linkam brochure v1.54 (2026) fetched: it carries no body dimensions, only 22 mm sample size, 15 mm XY, 4.8 mm working distance.

geometry.notes: Sources: OptistatDry BLV manual MAN-OPTDRY-BLV-2.1.0 Sep 2017 (andor.oxinst.com; robots.txt blocked scripts/v5_snapshot.py so it was fetched with WebFetch and text-extracted with pypdf into the scratchpad), OptistatDry brochure doc 4694 (2018) 'Cool down time from ambient to 4.2 K < 160 minutes at 50 Hz; Typical cooling power 0.2 W at 4.2 K; Optical access 28 mm diameter clear view, f1', Optistat matrix PDF (research/v5/cache/c73e273061693731.txt) and QD-Oxford product page (research/v5/cache/295cbbaf14723ca3.txt). Geometry: vertical cryostat body (OVC with SHI 101D two-stage GM cold head on top, He gas lines entering at the rear), narrowing to an 80 mm optical window block tail at the bottom with four radial window ports (f/1, 28 mm clear view) and one axial port underneath (blanked as standard); each OVC window held by an O-ring and 4 M3 nylon screws, with a matching radiation-shield window/blank held by a spring clip. Radiation shield is cooled by the GM first stage and carries the charcoal sorb on its removable front plate; sample platform/puck bolts to the heat exchanger on the GM second stage. Whole cryostat hangs in a stand with two side panels, cradle on four anti-vibration mounts (M6, 25 mm fine height adjust) and radial restraints in the OVC T-slots. Standard wiring here is the 12-track PCB puck (12P code); the alternative LX20 20-pin option (nine constantan twisted pairs + one copper pair) is not part of this configuration. Vibration <10 um RMS at the sample. Cooldown RT to base ~3.0 h (DC12 puck). Temperature control by Mercury iTC (450 W).

evidence.collected_by: research agent v3 (WebSearch found the andor.oxinst.com download listing 'OptistatDry TLEX User Guide'; PDF at /downloads/uploads/ read with tavily_extract)

evidence.location: Section 5.8 Sample changing (approx. p. 36-37); see also Section 5.1 Loading the sample probe ('pump and flush the sample space one more time, leaving one atmosphere of helium gas')
evidence.quote: To remove the probe, flush the sample space with clean, dry helium gas, maintaining a positive pressure (just above 1 atmosphere) on the VTI pump-and-flush valve.
evidence.reasoning: purge.gas = 'Sample chamber can be purged with gas (dry gas purge against condensation)'. The TLEX manual instructs flushing the sample space with dry helium at positive pressure so moisture and contaminants stay out while the probe is removed, through a dedicated pump-and-flush valve. This satisfies the any-of requirement vacuum.available/purge.gas for the TLEX, whose vacuum.available is stored as false.
evidence.review_status: independently re-fetched and verified by a second agent: TLEX manual PDF re-fetched (HTTP 200; Issue 3.0, July 2019). Quote verbatim in Sec. 5.8 Sample changing (top of p. 37). Sec. 5.1 confirms 'pump and flush the sample space one more time, leaving one atmosphere of helium gas' (five-nines He advised). Sec. 4.4 blanks the port 'to prevent moisture and other contaminants from getting into the sample space'. The NW16 VTI sample-space pump-and-flush valve is standard, so installed/true fits 'sample chamber can be purged with gas'. A sealed dry-He space meets the frost any-of intent.

evidence.claim: OptistatDry TLEX sample holder dimensions are 19 mm x 30 mm (in a 20 mm diameter sample tube); the 19 mm width bounds the diameter of a sample mounted on the standard holder.
evidence.collected_by: research agent v3 (tavily_extract of the qd-oxford product page comparison table; matrix PDF p. 3 checked)

evidence.location: Optistat Model Comparison table, row 'Sample holder dims', column OptistatDry TLEX (5th value; column order DN, DN-V, CF, CF-V, Dry TLEX, Dry BLV)
evidence.quote: Sample holder dims | 19 mm x 30 mm | 20 mm x 50 mm | 19 mm x 30 mm | 20 mm x 50 mm | 19 mm x 30 mm | 20 mm x 50 mm
evidence.reasoning: No explicit maximum sample diameter is published. The holder width (19 mm) is the binding, conservative sample-diameter limit and is consistent with the 20 mm sample tube (row 'Maximum sample space 20 mm Ø'). The specification matrix PDF p. 3 prints this TLEX cell as '119 mm x 30 mm', an evident typo because a holder cannot exceed the 20 mm tube, so the product-page value of 19 mm is used. 19 mm = 19000 um. Medium confidence because holder width is mapped to sample diameter.
evidence.review_status: independently re-fetched and verified by a second agent: Live product page 'Sample holder dims' for OptistatDry TLEX = 19 mm x 30 mm. The live R5 matrix p. 3 prints '119 mm x 30 mm', a typo since the tube is 20 mm. The DN/CF X models specify the same holder ('19 mm wide x 30 mm long'). 19000 um is below the 20 mm tube. Holder width -> max sample diameter is an interpretation and a near upper bound, so a requirement right at about 19 mm is marginal. Accepted at medium confidence; inferred_estimate would be the more cautious status.

evidence.claim: The standard classic PPMS purges its sample chamber with clean gas through the built-in vent and flush valves (Purge/Seal operation). By default the gas is helium boil-off from the dewar; another clean gas can be connected to the Sample Vent-Up port.

evidence.quote: The vent valve allows helium gas into the sample chamber during venting and purging procedures. A purging procedure vents the sample chamber with clean gas and pumps it out through the flush valve, and then repeats the same process two more times.

evidence.review_status: independently re-fetched and verified by a second agent: The quote matches 1070-150 Rev. B5 sec. 3.4 (p. 3-7). Appendix A.3.18/A.3.19 confirm that the Model 6000 vent/flush valves vent and purge the chamber with dewar helium boil-off, or with another gas on the Sample Vent-Up port. Purge/Seal is a step of the standard sample-installation procedure, so installed is correct. A dry-helium purge removes air and moisture before cooling, which is the anti-condensation sense of the key.

geometry.notes: Vertical cryogen-free PPMS: a single Cryomech two-stage pulse tube sits in helium gas in a 'bucket' tank (not vacuum-mounted); first stage ~45 K cools the main and annulus radiation shields and cryopump stage 1; the second stage condenses He onto a ~150 cc LHe pool that cools the 4 K Plate by thermosiphon; the switch-less 14 T NbTi solenoid is conduction-cooled by solid contact to the 4 K Plate and produces a vertical (longitudinal) field at 120 A full field. The sample chamber (2.5 cm clear bore) runs down the magnet bore; 4.2 K helium from the bucket passes a counter-flow heat exchanger and mass-flow controller (0-5000 sccm) into the cooling annulus around the chamber and returns via the circulation scroll pump (5-50 Torr return, 500-800 Torr outlet), giving 1.8-400 K at the puck. The puck (2.3 cm Cu, Au plated) plugs into the 12-pin keyed connector at the chamber bottom; the block thermometer is clamped to the puck interface outside the chamber. Magnet centre 4.05 cm above puck surface; 14 T uniformity +/-0.1% over 5.5 cm on axis. Options modelled: ETO (2 channels), VSM (linear transport motor on the top KF flange, 6.3 mm coil bore, 9 mm coil separation, 40 Hz x 2 mm) and Heat Capacity (3 x 3 mm platform, puck microcalorimeter in high vacuum via the integrated cryopump). No optical windows in this configuration (magneto-optic FOSH option not installed). Outer dimensions are D x W x H for cryostat plus can rack; the 67x70x100 cm electronics cabinet and 69x50x62 cm compressor stand apart. 14 T startup 40 h typical; puck 300 K to 1.9 K in under 40 min.

geometry.notes: ILL pool unit 82ILHV100: 'Type | Orange Ø100', 'Quad-exchanger', 1.5-320 K, Ø100 x 265 mm sample space, aluminium A5-AG3 in beam, top loading for high-pressure measurements. Wet cryostat: LN2 bath + LHe bath, cold valve + capillary to the heat exchanger, He vapour drawn through the annulus to a roots/rotary pump for <4.2 K (ISIS: 2 psi feed, 50 ohm 100 W max heater, cooldown 3.5-4 h for 100 mm, 10-15 min from 20 K to 1.5 K). ILL manual: sample chamber pumped with a primary pump then 20 cc helium exchange gas admitted via blue 3-way valve; isolation vacuum pumped <1e-5 with a turbo. AS Scientific has built the Orange under ILL licence since 1981 (ILL history page); 2015 exchanger modification 'operates three times faster'. Outer-dimension values above are from NIST's 100 mm Orange (same ILL design) and are a top-flange-to-beam distance and the well bore only; the renderer should treat vessel/tail diameters as unpublished. geometry.notes: attoDRY2100 with the optional 9 T solenoid and the Basic Measurement Insert (art. 1007005). Pulse-tube closed-cycle magneto-optical cryostat, 1.65-300 K automated, base 1.65-1.8 K for standard inserts, stability < ±10 mK guaranteed (1.5-10 K), > 1 mW at 2 K at the sample, full 9 T available at 300 K, initial cooldown 20-24 h incl. 9 T magnet, sample cooldown 3-5 h. Sample sits in He exchange gas inside a top-loading probe bore (49 mm / 49.7 mm per brochure); optical access only via the insert's single 25 mm uncoated fused-silica top window. Pulse-tube identification is explicit on the product page ('mechanical vibrations created by the pulse-tube coldhead are decoupled'), but no cold-head model or valve frequency is published for this model, so the rate is omitted. Cached sources: research/v5/cache/465c82dd2b1ea577.txt (datasheet 1009389), 1712f2e73b097b95.txt (product page), 080be7f40dfda0d5.txt (Basic Measurement Insert page), 3a645da2483eab24.txt (attoDRY brochure, '49.7 mm diameter probe bore fitting all attocube inserts').

geometry.notes: Basic (standard) shroud configuration: room-temperature objective (max. outer diameter 36 mm) looks down through a single 25 mm fused-silica top window; cold shield lid adjustable for a 3.5 mm minimum working distance; lid carries 88x M6 holes on a 12.5 mm grid and 30/60 mm cage threads; feedthrough ring with blind flanges included (DC/SMA/fiber optional); not compatible with positioners. Base temp 3.5-3.8 K per shroud page, 3.8-320 K per spec sheet; cooldown < 4.5 h to 5 K; cooling power > 170 mW @ 5 K; vibration < 5 nm p-p vertical. Pulse-tube identification and the 1 Hz valve rate come from Vadia et al., PRX Quantum 2, 040318 (2021) (arXiv:2103.05619, co-authored by attocube), which also reports '1 Hz periodic pattern of mechanical pulses characteristic of closed-cycle coolers'; attocube's own pages only call it a 'closed-cycle cryostat' with 'cryocooler assembly ... underneath'. Permanent-magnet shroud exists as a custom option only; no magnet in this configuration. Cached sources: research/v5/cache/5295d024c2d737cc.txt (spec), 4b7ada6b9903adcb.txt (Basic shroud), 5039eed9ac55d4ca.txt (product page), 3a645da2483eab24.txt (brochure), 1a4d6faca33fc8fd.txt (arXiv).

geometry.notes: Single source: BINDER MKFT 240 product page, snapshot research/v5/cache/87f30350de2c404b.txt (fetched 2026-10-31; no earlier cache existed). Standard configuration article 9020-0383 (MKFT240-400V, 400 V / 50 Hz, 6 kW, 16 A, 67 dB(A), 415 kg empty). Geometry: 1115 W x 1940 H x 925 D mm housing box on 4 castors (two with brakes), single front door with heated viewing window and LED lighting; inner stainless steel chamber 735 W x 700 H x 443 D mm = 228 L with 1 rack standard (6 max). The only sample-wiring route fitted as standard is the 50 mm silicone-plugged access port on the left wall; the page lists no electrical feedthrough or line count, so wiring is recorded as that one port (count 1 = ports, not conductors). Optional ports (30/80/100/125 mm left/right/top, 100 x 35 mm door notch) are NOT fitted in this configuration. Thermal: -70 to +180 C (203.15 to 453.15 K), humidity 10-98 % RH only between 10 and 95 C; heating 5.0 K/min (-40 to 180 C), cooling 4.2 K/min (180 to -40 C), 180 to -70 C in 110 min; uniformity 0.2-1.8 K, fluctuation 0.1-0.5 K. Cooling is a cascade compressor unit (R-452A / R-23) with 20 L internal water tank for vapour humidification; no cryogen. No stage plates exist in this archetype: 'stages' records the chamber air-temperature set-point extremes. Viewing-window size, fan speed and compressor speed are not published on the page; no datasheet PDF was found linked on it. For the 3D model: box with front door; animate door hinge, compressor hum and chamber air flow; the LED-lit window is on the door, size unknown, so do not invent a diameter.

Geometry from Cryomech drawing CH1A600 rev A (supersedes CH10600): 241.3 mm room-temperature flange; 267.7 mm motor housing with two eyebolts above the flange; 127 mm diameter cold cylinder 307.8 mm long below the flange ending in a bare copper heat exchanger (8x M10 on 101.6 mm BC). Geometry for the 3D model: an 813 mm wide, 1257 mm tall cylinder (liftover height 40 in / 1016 mm per the same sheet) with an offset 317 mm neck; inside, a 731 mm diameter cavity with a 52 L LN2 pool under a turn-tray and 676 mm of usable height above it filled by 12 square racks (12 shelves of 100-cell boxes) plus 4 mini racks, two Pt-1000 probes in a central three-tube sensor assembly. The catalog's primary document (bsilab, ML-CRYO0032 E, 2015) was used for consistency with the catalog values (370 L, 676 mm, 1257 mm); the current MVE sheet ML-000019 Rev 0 (https://mvebio.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/4/2025/01/MVE-HEco-800-Series-Spec-Sheet-091024.pdf) gives 360 L w/o inventory, 673 mm usable height, 1350 mm overall (TS model), 1038 mm liftover, 218 kg empty / 526 kg full. geometry.notes: CG-400 = SPEX item 6875 (same 52x55x46 cm, 20 kg specs appear in the SPEX 14th Edition Handbook p.49 for the 6875). Single grinding chamber in the lid: a dual-electromagnet coil housing hangs into an insulated LN2 tub; the closed vial sits inside the coil, fully immersed, and the steel impactor is shuttled magnetically end-to-end at the programmed cps (the mill's only moving part; the user-facing 'rate' is back-and-forth cycles per second, so 10 cps = 20 impacts/s per the sibling 6770 manual, https://isolab.ess.washington.edu/resources/manuals/SPEX_Cryo_Mill.pdf). LN2 level sensor shuts the mill down when low; auto-fill (6875A/CG-450) is NOT fitted in this configuration. Touchscreen controller stores 20 programs, dual USB. No vacuum, no magnet spec, no sample electrical connections. Render: box cabinet with lid, LN2 pool at 77 K with boil-off vapour, one cylindrical vial in a coil with an oscillating impactor (8-15 Hz).

geometry.notes: Two sources only, both ESPEC North America: the 2-page ADBC-T flyer (research/v5/cache/0adc2434242b8421.raw, an image-only PDF read visually; its .txt is empty) and the Battery Test Systems family page (research/v5/cache/ba9022fb6a6fdaa3.txt), which repeats the flyer spec table verbatim; quotes are taken from the family-page text where available. Flyer-only numbers: Weight Approx. 1,455 lbs (660 kg); Floor load capacity of the chamber (Equally distributed load) 88 lbs (40 kg). Geometry for the 3D model: a single 1200 W x 1300 D x 2022 H mm floor-standing box; three equal 510 x 400 x 400 mm zones stacked vertically behind three slate-blue front doors with screw-in lock knobs; a shorter blue panel below them fronting the refrigeration/machinery bay (flyer photo shows a finned condenser unit at the base and louvred side/top vents); a full-height black control column on the right with three zone controllers (one per zone), status lamps and a red emergency-stop button. Each zone rear wall carries a grid of round cable ports (flyer photo) for the user-supplied charge/discharge power supply; the ADBC-T itself has no instrumentation lines, so wiring kind is 'none'. Horizontal laminar airflow per zone (blower/plenum behind the rear wall; no CFM published). Cooling: 'Independent control of three chambers' plus a 'Water-cooled refrigeration system' option and the condenser unit in the flyer photo establish a mechanical refrigeration system; the standard condenser type, compressor count and refrigerant are not published (catalog flags cryogen fields unknown). No window is listed as standard or option; no vacuum, no magnet. Options not fitted in this configuration: pressure relief vent, gas detector, CO2 fire extinguisher, impedance measurement function, custom battery mounting boards, water-cooled refrigeration. Tavily quota was exhausted; WebSearch found no additional ADBC-T spec source (ESPEC NA has no separate ADBC-T model page).

geometry.notes: Two sources only, both ESPEC North America (snapshots research/v5/cache/c98e1451f190c129.txt = model page, research/v5/cache/d57669701effc740.txt = Platinous J brochure Feb 2026). Exterior dimensions disagree slightly: model page 973 x 1220 x 1930 mm vs brochure 973 x 1184 x 1934 mm; the model page (catalog primary document) values are used. Floor-standing stainless box cabinet on heavy-duty casters with one front door; stainless workspace 500 x 600 x 750 mm (225 L) with rounded corners and one wire shelf. Thermal system per brochure cutaway (p.3): a blower at the rear recirculates air across a cooling coil, heaters and an in-chamber heated humidity bath (labels: 'Test Area, Blower, Heaters, Cooling Coil, Humidity Bath, Air Flow'); mechanical refrigeration with electronic expansion valves, no cryogen in standard configuration (LN2 boost is an unfitted option). -70 to 180 C, 10-98 %RH, 6 C/min heating, 4 C/min cooling, 400 CFM, 208/230 V 3ph 40 A, 25,000 BTU/h heat to room, 76 dBA. No vacuum, no magnet. Standard configuration has no window (viewing window option 9 x 10.3 in not fitted); the only sample pass-through is a single 4 in cable port centred in the left wall with two flexible plugs. For the 3D model: box with front door, conditioning plenum (blower, heaters, coil, humidity bath) behind/above the test area, air circulating through the workspace, a 4 in round port on the left wall, 10-inch touchscreen GL controller on the cabinet, 1/2 in condensate drain hose. Refrigeration machinery is below the workspace behind hinged service panels (height not published).

geometry.notes: Compact ultra-low-temperature stirred-liquid metrology bath, -80 C to 100 C, cascade refrigeration with two 1/4 HP compressors and a 500 W heater; 1700 VA at 115 V/60 Hz or 230 V/50 Hz. Outer box 305 W x 762 H x 610 D mm, 52 kg, casters fitted. The 4 L stainless-steel tank sits under an insulated lid carrying the stirring motor (under a motor cover), the control PRT in a small hole, and the 83 x 114 mm rectangular access hole with an insulated access cover the user may drill for probe fixtures; max immersion 180 mm. Fluid level 12 to 50 mm below tank top. Back panel: circuit breaker, IEC power inlet, drain valve, RS-232 connector, removable vent panel. Stability +/-0.006 C and uniformity +/-0.008 C at -80 C (ethanol); cooling 25 C to -80 C in 130 min. Source discrepancies: the current Fluke product page gives Access Opening 86 x 114 mm, Depth 178 mm and 'Size (WxDxH) 305 x 610 x 762 mm' vs the User's Guide 83 x 114 mm / 180 mm (the catalog capabilities use 83 mm and 178 mm); the catalog description's 'two 1/2 HP compressors' is not supported by the manual, which says 'Two 1/4 HP compressors'. The User's Guide PDF is robots-blocked for scripts/v5_snapshot.py; text was extracted from a WebFetch-saved copy. Product page snapshot: research/v5/cache/a3d05ea0d7cbcd34.txt.

That PDF's original URL now returns 404 and the current copy at https://kiutra.com/resources/l-type-rapid-installation-requirements is gated behind a contact form, so the figures were recovered from the search-engine index of the document, not read directly from the file; treat them as lower-confidence than the other quotes. geometry.notes: Single source: LACO product page X-1P33958 (snapshot research/v5/cache/73755b639f2ae981.txt). Horizontal 17.5 in DIA x 24 in stainless cylinder with hinged front door carrying a 6 in viewport, and a rear machined bulkhead carrying 8 x DB25 + 4 x DB9 feedthroughs (8*25 + 4*9 = 236 pins). LN2-cooled pillow-plated cylindrical shroud, LN2 door shroud and LN2 platen, all rated -150 C (123.15 K); no heaters listed so no upper temperature. Platen slides out on a linear rail. Inside working envelope 16.0 in DIA x 22 in D, capacity up to 6U CubeSat. Pumping: 8.5 CFM dry scroll + high-vacuum turbo (turbo speed not published). Vacuum 1e-6 Torr; leak rate 1e-8 atm cc/s He. Other ports: NW16, NW25, NW40, ISO100, CF2.75, LN2 feedthrough. HVC-3500 controller with 7 in touch screen on the mobile cart. Cart/enclosure dimensions not published on this page or the sibling 18x24 chiller page (research/v5/cache/a4d07d242f93a9cc.txt); Tavily quota was exhausted so no wider brochure search was possible. The sibling chiller SKU lists a 16 in x 22 in platen, but that is a different system and was not carried over. For the 3D model: chamber diameter 17.5 in doubles as outer height because the cart height is unknown; the viewport is on the door at the cylinder's front end-cap, not the side wall.

Only visible motion is the cryogen flow (1.1 L/h LHe at 5 K) and the external vacuum pump the datasheet says every cryostat requires ('Each cryostat requires a pump to operate'); the cryostat body itself has no moving parts and is specified at <12 nm vibration and 2 nm/min drift at 4 K. Stability (+/-50 mK) and base pressure (~1e-5 Torr) are typical, not guaranteed. Window materials offered: UV fused silica, ZnSe, sapphire, CaF2 (top and bottom); bottom may be a blank plate. geometry.notes: Static pour-fill LN2 cryostat: no cryocooler, no pump inside the cryostat, no magnet; the only motion is LN2 boil-off vapour from the 400 mL top reservoir. Configured without VPF-PM pumping manifold so range is 77-500 K. Weight 3.3 kg (7 lb). The instrumentation adapter (brochure) carries a 10-pin electrical feedthrough, three spare o-ring sealed ports, an evacuation valve and a pressure relief valve; the wired variant WH-10P gives 10 PhBr twisted pairs. The stage temperature_K values are the 77 K base (both reservoir and mount sit at LN2 temperature when not heated). Window material default is fused silica (WR-STD-FS); sapphire, ZnSe, CaF2, KBr, TPX are 3 mm or 6 mm options.

geometry.notes: Bench-top cryogen-free probe station: 654 x 676 mm footprint with a 203 mm OD x 132 mm tall electroless-nickel aluminum vacuum chamber, 152 mm top opening, 63.5 mm fused-quartz top viewport (54 mm viewing), inner radiation shield (132 mm lid, 50 mm IR-absorbing window). Two-stage CCR: 1st stage cools the radiation shield (catalog cross-section labels 35 K), 2nd stage cools the sample stage (10 K base with 6 arms; 8 K with 2, 9 K with 4). Six micro-manipulated probe arms anchored to the shield with ZN50 probe bases braid-anchored to the sample stage (probes ~18 K / <20 K). Cooldown 3.5 h, warmup 2.25 h, 6.25 h cycle. Vibration at sample <2 um. The CCR is tagged cryogen_free_gm as the closest enum: Lake Shore does not name the cold head technology, so the GM displacer motion is not sourced and is listed in not_found rather than in moving_parts. Ring magnet kit (PS-RING-MAG-KIT) and PS-HTSTAGE are not fitted in this configuration. Field horizontal, parallel to sample plane; homogeneity '0.6% over 10 mm diameter; 2.6% over 25 mm diameter'. Vacuum <1e-5 Torr at He base; ports NW40 pump, NW25 gauge, 0.25 in NPT gas. Cycle: 0.5 h pump, 1.25 h cooldown, 1.25 h warmup. Vibration <300 nm. cryogen set to lhe_flow; LN2 flow is the alternative mode through the same transfer line (catalog cryogen.type lists both). Probe electrical types (DC/RF, microwave to 67 GHz, fiber optic) are per-order, so no fixed coax/DC/fibre count is published. geometry.notes: Sources: Lake Shore FWPX technical-specifications page (cache research/v5/cache/9ae700052f15978d.txt) and Lake Shore Probe Stations catalog PDF probestationcatalog_l.pdf pp. 38-39 (cache research/v5/cache/75efd8eb8da79422.txt), whose cross-section diagram labels 'Radiation shield stage (20 K) / Sample stage (4.5 K) / Probe (25 K) / Probe arm base / Probe arm shield / Thermal anchors / Vacuum chamber base'. Scene geometry: a 406 mm OD x 178 mm tall nickel-plated aluminium vacuum chamber (330 mm top opening, 102 mm fused-quartz top viewport with 91 mm viewing area, NW40 pump port with isolation valve, NW25 gauge port, 0.25 in NPT gas port, 3.5 kPa relief valve) on a 1067 x 851 mm platform; inside, a nickel-plated aluminium radiation shield with 180 mm lid and 159 mm IR-absorbing window (152 mm viewing area) surrounds the 4.5 K x-y translating sample stage carrying a 102 mm grounded SH-4.00-G sample holder; six micromanipulated probe arms enter from the sides, arm anchored to the 20 K shield, probe anchored to the sample stage. Cooling is a 2-stage continuous-flow cryostat (sample + radiation shield) fed by a large-bore S-style LHe/LN2 transfer line with 12.7 mm top-port Dewar withdrawal; no compressor or cold head, so the only mechanical motion is cryogen flow, the pump, and operator-driven stage/probe moves. Base 4.5 K with up to 6 arms (3.5 K with PS-LT, not fitted); control range 5-475 K on the current web page (4.5-420 K in the catalog PDF); cooldown 1.5 h, warmup 1.5 h, cycle 3.5 h, vibration <30 nm, base pressure <1e-5 Torr, no magnet option, no backside optical access. The 'lhe_flow' enum covers both cryogens: the same flow circuit runs on LN2 (80 K) or LHe (5 K).

geometry.notes: Standard LTS420 (non-E) with T96-S controller and LNP96-S LN2 pump. Geometry: a flat 166 x 90 x 24 mm stage body (Linkam spec page; McCrone lists an older '160 x 80 x 24 mm') carrying a 53.5 x 43 mm silver block; swing-out lid with a standard 18 mm viewing aperture (Bioimager, Linkam distributor; 35/50 mm on request); inner lid for stability. Window count 2 = top lid window plus a lower window inferred only from 'Can be used with transmitted or reflected light' and the published condenser working distance of 12.5 mm; the lower aperture size is not published. Stage body is water-cooled for work above 300 C (brochure). Objective min working distance 6.5 mm, condenser 12.5 mm. Temperature < -195 C (78 K) to 420 C, stability < 0.01 C, rates 0.01-50 C/min. LN2 is pumped from the LNP96 dewar by the control unit's pumps (T96-controlled) and injected directly into the block; the T96 drives the Pt100 sensor and heater. No electrical sample lines in this configuration (LTS420E variants add 2-pin LEMO/BNC/probes). Brochure quotes come from Linkam's own 'Download PDF Product Brochure' link on https://www.linkam.co.uk/lts420-brochure (Google Drive id 1wbj1pLk89eX-y2dWxbxm_mYzIBILZAab, v1.18 2026); v5_snapshot could not cache it (robots.txt), text extracted locally.
